title: Vegan Caesar Salad
subtitle: Crisp cos with a creamy cashew Caesar dressing and crispy capers
excerpt: A fully plant-based Caesar using soaked cashews blended with garlic, lemon, Dijon and nutritional yeast to stand in for anchovies and parmesan. Crispy capers provide the savoury hit.
sourceNotes: Vegan Caesar variants became widespread in UK and US food media from the 2010s as plant-based cooking gained mainstream attention. The cashew-base dressing is the most common approach, popularised by vegan bloggers and cookbooks including Oh She Glows and Minimalist Baker. Nutritional yeast as a parmesan substitute is documented across vegan cookery from the mid-2010s.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Soak the cashews overnight if possible. The dressing keeps for 4 days in the fridge.

glossaryTerms.definition: Deactivated yeast sold as flakes or powder, with a savoury, slightly cheesy flavour. Used in vegan cooking as a substitute for parmesan or other hard cheeses.

content.text: Vegan Caesar replaces the egg yolk and anchovy of the original with soaked cashews, blended smooth with lemon, garlic, Dijon and a spoonful of capers for their brine. The result is a thick, creamy dressing with genuine depth. Crispy capers, fried in a little olive oil, replace the anchovy saltiness on the plate.
Soak the cashews for at least 2 hours, or overnight. Cold water is fine; hot water works in 30 minutes if you are short of time. The longer the soak, the smoother the blend.

items.prepNote: soaked in cold water for 2 hours, drained

content.text: Put the drained cashews, {{garlic}} of garlic, the juice of {{lemon}} lemon, {{dijon-mustard}} of Dijon mustard, {{worcestershire-sauce}} of Worcestershire sauce, {{nutritional-yeast}} of

, {{water}} of water and {{sea-salt-fine}} of salt in a blender. Blend on high for 1 to 2 minutes until completely smooth. Taste and adjust the lemon or salt. The dressing should pour from a spoon in a thick ribbon.

Heat {{olive-oil}} of olive oil in a frying pan over medium-high heat. Add the dried {{capers}} of capers and fry for 2 to 3 minutes until they burst and crisp up. Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper. In the same pan, add the bread cubes and fry for 4 minutes, turning, until golden. Drain on paper.
Toss the cos leaves in a large bowl with enough dressing to coat each leaf. Divide across four plates. Top with croutons and crispy capers. Serve immediately with any remaining dressing on the side.

items.cause: Cashews not soaked long enough, or blender not powerful enough.
items.fix: Soak for at least 2 hours in cold water. A high-powered blender makes a smoother result than a standard jug blender. Blend for an extra minute.
Add more lemon juice a teaspoon at a time, tasting between additions. A little more salt often helps too.

items.cause: Heat too high or capers not dry enough.
items.fix: Pat the capers very dry before frying. Use medium-high heat, not full heat. They take about 2 to 3 minutes once the oil is hot.

content.text: The cashew Caesar is one of the better arguments for plant-based cooking: it does what it says it does. The dressing is creamy and savoury, and tastes nothing like the low-fat bottled versions of the original. The crispy capers are the detail that makes it work on the plate, giving the salt and texture hit that anchovies provide in the classic.
